title: Mandumah platform v2 (experiment 47)
description_html: The scan is the bottom layer: every value points at Azure's words on the page (ink_anchors; open ink links to see the crop). Each run's reading of a document is its own version, side by side; one is shown. Printed values are never overwritten: corrections, misprints and D33 changes are readings beside the print. «المرجع السابق» resolves to the first full citation; citation_links holds real links only. Schema diagram: /diagram/schema47.html. Built by experiments/47_platform_v2 (load47.py, link47.py) from the same sources as platform.db; read only.

storage_roots.description: A place files live (local disk, an S3 bucket), so the database stores keys relative to it, never absolute paths. [Provenance and identity]

columns.base: path or s3://bucket/prefix in this environment

runs.description: One processing run (a Gemini/Argon reading, a judge pass, a final rebuild, an exam): what it ran with and what it cost. [Provenance and identity]

columns.kind: sample | base | judged | final | exam | replay
columns.parent_run: the run whose readings this one builds on

load_events.description: One execution of the loader or linker, so every row can be traced to the load that wrote it. [Provenance and identity]

model_calls.description: Every paid model call ever made for a run (from gemini_spend.jsonl, raw chunk files, judge answers), so the cost of any page, article or verdict adds up. [Provenance and identity]

columns.job: job: read | retry | judge | title | numbers ...

actors.description: Who (which person, agent, model or code rule) made an assertion, a patch or a review. [Provenance and identity]

id_registry.description: The append-only register of public ids (A persons, I institutions, C cited works), so a rebuild gives every entity the same id again. [Provenance and identity]

merged_ids.description: When two ids turn out to be one thing (or one splits), the retired id points to the survivor so no link or bookmark breaks. [Provenance and identity]

documents.description: One file in the archive (an article PDF or one part of a thesis): where it is and how far it has been processed. [The ink layer]

columns.part_label: thesis part suffix: T A C F 1..n O R
columns.part_kind: article | title-page | abstract | contents | chapter | conclusion | references
columns.level: legacy-pdf | azure | structured | judged | final | person-checked

pages.description: One scanned page: its size, image, printed folio and running head, and Azure's own confidence on it. [The ink layer]

columns.printed_folio_int: from the role.pageNumber region (evidence for page ranges)

azure_lines.description: One line as Azure read it (its "P:N" label), with its box and the span of Azure word numbers on it; kept only for structured documents. [The ink layer]

columns.line_no: N in the 'P:N' labels of flags, patches, judge targets and fixes
columns.last_word: Azure word ordinals on the page

ink_anchors.description: An exact place on the scan (a page and a span of Azure words, or a box) that any value can cite as its evidence: "show me the ink". [The ink layer]

columns.method: words | line | box | page  (how precisely the value was placed)

anchor_links.description: Extra evidence places for a value that needs more than one (a citation running across two pages, a name printed twice). [The ink layer]

columns.owner_kind: citation_mention | byline_mention | assertion | correction | flag | finding | patch | quran | figure ...

versions.description: One reading of one document by one run; every content and quality row belongs to one of these, and one per document is shown. [The reading layer]

columns.stamp_run: what the stamp file says (it can disagree with the folder)
columns.content_in_db: 0 = retired to files; the row and its hashes stay

line_map.description: Translation between a run's ALTO line ids and Azure's lines, so a flag, patch or fix given as "4:2" lands on the right block. [The reading layer]

columns.azure_line_no: NULL when the ALTO line has no Azure source (rare)
columns.region_id: exactly one of them is set

sections.description: The article's headings as a tree, so a search hit or a citation can say which section it sits in. [The reading layer]

blocks.description: The text in reading order exactly as printed (D30), one row per paragraph, heading, cell, note paragraph or verse group, with its quality roll-up. [The reading layer]

columns.block_id: the run's JATS/ALTO id, e.g. p1b9
columns.role: closed list: title | title-translated | byline | affiliation | abstract | keywords | heading | paragraph | list-item | footnote | endnote | ref | caption | table-cell | verse-group | quote | front-matter | back-matter
columns.text_source: reader | rule | patch:<source>:<patch_key> (source = person | judge | gemini-retry)

block_parts.description: Where each piece of a block sits on each page it spans (1,733 blocks cross a page). [The reading layer]

page_regions.description: Ink on the page that is not article text (running heads, page numbers, noise, show-through, the next article, picture text), kept so every leave-out can be checked. [The reading layer]

columns.role: pageHeader | pageNumber | pageFooter | noise | pictureText | pictureJunk | formulaInk | ornament | showThrough | otherArticle

notes.description: One footnote or endnote, with its printed label and its place on the page. [The reading layer]

note_calls.description: Each call mark in the running text, where it is, and whether it found its note. [The reading layer]

note_call_targets.description: The note or notes one call opens ("(٤، ٩)" opens two). [The reading layer]

figures.description: Each picture, table and equation as an object: its box, crop, caption, Arabic and English descriptions, text inside it, LaTeX and MathML. [The reading layer]

columns.figure_id: JATS id; inline formulas get an anchor-based id

table_cells.description: Tables as data: every cell with its row, column and spans, so a table can be rebuilt, exported or queried. [The reading layer]

verse_lines.description: Each printed verse line, or hemistich where the print separates them, as printed with its vowels, so poetry can be searched and cited line by line. [The reading layer]

columns.poet_hint: as printed near the verse («قال المتنبي»), not resolved

text_corrections.description: The text-correction ledger: every word where Azure's reading, the print and a proposed correction differ (Azure misreadings fixed in the text; suspected misprints kept as printed, D30), with who said so and why. [The reading layer]

columns.azure_wc: what Azure read, and how sure it was
columns.printed: what the paper says (the text shown)
columns.proposed: misprint only: the suggested correction, never applied to the text

search_units.description: One searchable piece of text (block, figure description, picture text, equation, verse line, printed citation), so one search covers everything and every hit opens its ink. [The reading layer]

columns.uid: = blocks.uid for blocks; its own range for the rest
columns.unit_kind: block | alt-text | figure-text | equation | verse | citation
columns.stemmed: folded, with clitics و ب ل ف ك ال stripped

search_fts.description: FTS5 index over search_units (columns folded, stemmed); query it with MATCH 'stemmed : ' || stem47(:q) (plugin fold47)

catalogue_exports.description: Each MARC export marc.db was built from, so every catalogue value can be traced to its export and rechecked on the next one. [Bibliographic layer]

catalogue_records.description: Mandumah's catalogue entry, keyed by the stable 999$c, as it stands in one export. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.rec: position in that export only (trace back to the XML)
columns.type: 336 / Mandumah type: بحوث ومقالات | رسائل جامعية | بحوث المؤتمرات | عروض كتب

catalogue_record_documents.description: Which files the catalogue says belong to a record (a thesis has about ten parts); files may be absent from the bucket. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.stem: not a key into documents: 87,396 catalogued files are missing

publications.description: One scholarly item (article, thesis, conference paper, book review, editorial), whether we hold its scan or only its catalogue entry; the target of every real citation link. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.pub_id: 'W'+c999, or 'WS'+stem for an uncatalogued file (merged later via merged_ids)
columns.type: article | thesis | conference-paper | book-review | editorial | interview | report
columns.status: catalogued-only | pdf-only | azure | structured | judged | final | person-checked
columns.year_shown: denormalised from the chosen assertions, refreshed per release

metadata_assertions.description: Every value anyone gave for a bibliographic field (as printed, as corrected under D33, catalogue, Gemini title file, Qdrant payload, a person), with its place on the page; exactly one per field is chosen to show. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.field: title | title_translated | subtitle | pages | volume | issue | year | doi | journal_title | language ...
columns.form: printed | corrected | catalogue | gemini-title | qdrant-payload | html-view | azure | person
columns.source: masters | catalogue | s3-gemini-title | qdrant | judge | person | rule
columns.reason: D33: why the corrected form differs from the printed one
columns.supersedes: a correction points at the printed form it corrects
columns.chosen_rule: person > judge > D33-corrected > printed > catalogue > gemini-title > qdrant

publication_dates.description: Every date of a publication in the calendar it was printed in, paired with its converted twin, and where it was read. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.pair_pk: its twin in the other calendar

languages.description: The language code list (ISO 639-2/B as key, with 639-1 and names in Arabic and English). [Bibliographic layer]

publication_languages.description: Which languages a publication is in, by role (text, abstract, title), and how we know. [Bibliographic layer]

abstracts.description: An abstract as printed or as catalogued, with its detected language and its place on the page. [Bibliographic layer]

keyword_terms.description: An author keyword as a term that can be counted across the archive. [Bibliographic layer]

publication_keywords.description: Which publication carries which keyword, as printed and from which source. [Bibliographic layer]

subject_terms.description: A catalogue subject heading or field of study, its Arabic and English forms as one term. [Bibliographic layer]

record_subjects.description: Which subjects the catalogue gives a record. [Bibliographic layer]

journals.description: One journal (Mandumah's journal code) with its country and the databases it is indexed in. [Bibliographic layer]

journal_titles.description: Every name a journal has had or been printed under, in which years, from which source. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.form: printed | running-head | catalogue | catalogue-en | romanised | person

journal_issns.description: Every ISSN string seen for a journal, cleaned and check-digit tested, with its ISSN-L. [Bibliographic layer]

publishers.description: A publisher (a university, society, ministry or press) as an entity. [Bibliographic layer]

journal_publishers.description: Which publisher published a journal, in which years. [Bibliographic layer]

issues.description: One physical issue of a journal, with its printed label, numbers, special/joint marks and both calendars. [Bibliographic layer]

issue_numbers.description: The issue numbers one physical issue covers (a joint issue "3,4" has two rows). [Bibliographic layer]

external_ids.description: Every outside identifier of a publication, journal, person, institution or cited work, and who assigned it. [Bibliographic layer]

columns.scheme: doi | c999 | 001 | issn-l | isbn | orcid | viaf | wikidata | ror | qdrant-doc | s3-key
columns.anchor_pk: a DOI printed on the page

role_codes.description: The controlled list of contributor roles (author, co-author, translator, reviewer of a book, editor, supervisor...). [People and institutions]

columns.code: author | coauthor | translator | reviewer | editor | supervisor | interviewer | compiler | original-author | editor-of-text (محقق)

persons.description: One real person, with an id that never changes across rebuilds. [People and institutions]

person_authorities.description: Which Mandumah authority ids belong to a person (a cataloguer's decision, our highest-trust identity signal); two when the catalogue has a duplicate. [People and institutions]

person_names.description: Every way a person's name is written (printed, catalogue heading, Latin form, cited form, initials), split into its Arabic name parts. [People and institutions]

columns.form_type: printed | catalogue-heading | catalogue-latin | cited | transliteration | initials | pseudonym

translit_pairs.description: Arabic↔Latin name-token pairs learned from the catalogue's own Latin headings (232k authority ids), used to match Latin bylines and citations and to search across scripts. [People and institutions]

byline_mentions.description: A name exactly as printed in one version's byline, with its titles («د.», «الشيخ») kept and its box on the scan; never changed by matching. [People and institutions]

columns.titles: د. | أ.د. | الشيخ | الدكتور ... (kept, not thrown away)

catalogue_contributors.description: Every contributor heading on a catalogue record (100/110/700), with its normalised role and authority id. [People and institutions]

authorships.description: One person's (or body's) part in one publication: role, position, and how we know who they are. [People and institutions]

columns.method: exact | token-subset | transliteration | script-twin | corporate | initials | catalogue-only | person

authorship_mentions.description: Joins the printed forms of a name (an Arabic and a Latin byline of the same author) to the one authorship they belong to. [People and institutions]

affiliation_mentions.description: An affiliation exactly as printed, split into position, department, faculty, organisation and place, with its box. [People and institutions]

affiliation_links.description: Which institution(s) a printed affiliation was matched to, with method, score and who said so. [People and institutions]

institutions.description: One university, faculty, department, ministry or centre, with a stable id and its parent. [People and institutions]

columns.kind: university | faculty | department | ministry | centre | society | press | committee
columns.catalogue_authority_id: corporate authority «مصر. جامعة القاهرة. كلية الحقوق»

institution_names.description: All names of an institution in Arabic, Latin and French, each typed; no single "primary" name (ROR style). [People and institutions]

columns.type: label | alias | acronym | printed | catalogue-heading | dissertation-502c

institution_relations.description: How institutions relate over time: part of, renamed to, successor of. [People and institutions]

supervisions.description: Who supervised whose thesis, where and when: the Arab world's academic family tree, from the catalogue. [People and institutions]

citation_mentions.description: Each place on a page where an article cites something (full citation, short form, «المرجع السابق»/«نفسه»/ibid./op. cit., Quran, hadith), with its ink and the first full citation it counts for. [Citations]

columns.mention_id: '<stem>|p<page>|w<first>-<last>|<n>': built on Azure word numbers, so it survives a new run
columns.reading_ord: order of the citation in the article's reading (note stream order)
columns.kind: full | short | ibid | op_cit | loc_cit | see_also | quran | hadith
columns.printed: the citation's own span, as printed
columns.printed_fixed: the same span with Azure misreadings fixed (what the linker also tries)
columns.parsed: JSON: authors, title, source, place, publisher, year, edition ...
columns.cited_pages: the locator: the page cited, not the work's pages

cited_works.description: One book, article, thesis, diwan or manuscript cited anywhere in the archive, the same whichever articles cite it, with its own times-cited even when it is not in Mandumah (most cited books are not). [Citations]

columns.pub_type: book | article | thesis | chapter | conference-paper | manuscript | diwan | web | quran | hadith-collection

cited_work_members.description: Which full citations were grouped into each cited work, why, and by whom; a person can move one with a patch. [Citations]

cited_work_authors.description: The authors of a cited work split into the parts of an Arabic name, tied to a person where the catalogue identifies them. [Citations]

link_runs.description: One pass of the linker: its code, thresholds and catalogue export, so any link can be reproduced. [Citations]

link_run_versions.description: Which versions one linker pass covered. [Citations]

citation_links.description: A REAL link only: a cited work found as a publication of the archive or catalogue (or an outside id), with status, score, method, evidence and who said so. No back-reference, no relation, no self-link. [Citations]

columns.via_mention_pk: the full mention whose text matched
columns.target_pub_id: scanned or catalogued-only: both are publications

work_relations.description: A typed relation between a cited work and another item (reviewed in, studied in, part of, edition or translation of), stored with its reverse, separate from citations. [Citations]

quran_ayat.description: A reference text of the Quran (sura, aya, text) to match quotations against; source and licence recorded. [Citations]

quran_citations.description: Every place an article quotes or cites the Quran, by sura and aya: a Quran citation index no other index has. [Citations]

flag_detectors.description: Each automatic check that raises flags, with its code version and thresholds, so "resolved" can be told from "new detector". [Quality]

flags.description: One warning raised by a code check on one version's page, tied to the detector that raised it and to its ink. [Quality]

columns.box_raw: as in the flag file ('2:1', 0-1000 box)

judge_calls.description: One look by one judge model and prompt at one page, kept even when it found nothing, with its cost. [Quality]

judge_findings.description: One problem a judge named on a page, with its route (auto, retry, human) and its ink. [Quality]

patches.description: One proposed correction (structure, text, metadata, who-is-who, citation grouping) from a person, the judge or a retry; never changed after it is made. [Quality]

columns.patch_key: '<run>|<stem>|<patch_id>' (upstream ids collide across a journal's articles)
columns.op: split_block | set_kind | replace_page_blocks | merge | split | assign-mention | set-parent | move-member | not-a-person ...
columns.payload_copy: only for person patches (they cannot be regenerated)

patch_applications.description: What happened to a patch in each build or rebuild that saw it (applied, skipped, overridden). [Quality]

columns.version_id: content patches: the version built; NULL for entity/citation patches

reviews.description: Every human or agent verdict on anything (a link, a resolution, a grouping, a finding, a flag, a correction, a page, a gold item): the ground truth trust scores are calibrated on. [Quality]

columns.subject_kind: link | relation | resolution | membership | authorship | finding | flag | correction | assertion | page | article
columns.subject_fingerprint: hash of what was seen, so a verdict re-attaches after rebuilds or is marked stale

catalogue_reports.description: A problem found in Mandumah's catalogue (or a print-vs-catalogue disagreement), with who is right, its evidence on the page, and whether Mandumah was told and fixed it in a later export. [Quality]

columns.kind: invalid-issn | stem-on-several-records | duplicate-001 | duplicate-authority | missing-author | name-differs | role-wrong | corporate-as-person | page-range | year | hijri-as-gregorian | title | language | author-count | missing-file | missing-record
columns.assert_pk: the D33 correction it rests on

vector_points.description: A link from each existing Qdrant point (mandumah_v2) to its document and, where offsets allow, its blocks, so a semantic hit opens the page and its payload counts as one more metadata reading. [Ties to what Mandumah already runs]

columns.stem: payload doc_id; not a key: points exist for documents we have not loaded

search_feedback.description: Users' feedback on Mandumah's AI search (from the ai_search_feedback MySQL dumps), as query/document judgements without user identities. [Ties to what Mandumah already runs]

columns.dump: the nightly dump it came from
columns.verdict: as the dump records it (columns fixed once the dump is inspected)
columns.user_hash: salted hash only; never names or emails

v_articles.description: Back-compat: the v46 `articles` row, shown for the current version of each document.

v_fixes.description: Back-compat: fixes and misprints of v46 are two slices of the ledger.

v_metadata_changes.description: D33 log: each corrected value beside the printed one it corrects.

v_catalogue_disagreements.description: Print vs catalogue, recomputed from the assertions (no stale snapshot).

v_mention_work.description: Each citation counted where it belongs: every mention (full or back-reference) of a work in one article.

v_times_cited.description: Times cited per cited work: citing publications (WoS headline) and all mentions incl. «المرجع السابق».

v_pub_times_cited.description: Times cited per archive/catalogue publication, through accepted best links only.

v_author_self_citations.description: True self-citation: an author of the citing publication is an author of the cited work (shared person id).

v_journal_citation_pairs.description: Journal self-citation and journal pairs (citation stacking), through accepted links.

v_block_trust.description: Trust of a block, from evidence (starting formula; calibrated on `reviews` per release): start at 1, x0.6 if any Azure word < 0.5, x0.9 per fix (max 3), x0.8 if a flag, x0.7 if patched by retry, floor 0.05.

v_judge_precision.description: Judge precision per model / prompt / finding type, against reviews: tells how far to trust an auto route.

v_flag_lifecycle.description: Flag lifecycle between two versions of one document, comparing only detectors present in both.

v_issue_coverage.description: Holdings per issue: catalogued vs in the bucket vs read — the map of what exists on paper but not in the index.

v_quran_index.description: Quran citation index: how often each aya is quoted or cited, by how many publications.

reconciliation_v46.description: Builder report: each table of platform.db (experiment 46), its v2 counterpart's count, and why they differ.

show_me_the_ink.title: Show me the ink: any citation of an article, with its crop of the scan
show_me_the_ink.description: Every citation mention of the shown version of one document, in reading order, with a link that draws the page and the box of Azure's words it was read from.
show_me_the_ink.sql:
SELECT m.reading_ord, m.container_id AS note, m.kind, m.marker, m.printed, m.cited_volume, m.cited_pages,
       t.printed AS counts_for_first_full_citation, m.resolve_method, m.unresolved_why, m.trust,
       a.anchor_key, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || m.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM citation_mentions m JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = m.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
LEFT JOIN citation_mentions t ON t.mention_pk = m.full_mention_pk
LEFT JOIN ink_anchors a ON a.anchor_pk = m.anchor_pk
WHERE v.stem = :stem ORDER BY m.reading_ord

back_references_resolved.title: «المرجع السابق» / «نفسه» / ibid. / op. cit. → the first full citation
back_references_resolved.description: Each back reference of an article and the first full citation of the work it counts for (chains collapsed); unresolved ones say why.
back_references_resolved.sql:
SELECT m.container_id AS note, m.kind, m.marker, m.printed AS back_reference, m.resolve_method,
       m.resolve_score, m.unresolved_why, t.container_kind || ':' || t.container_id AS first_full_in,
       t.printed AS first_full_citation, w.cited_work_id, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || m.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM citation_mentions m JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = m.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
LEFT JOIN citation_mentions t ON t.mention_pk = m.full_mention_pk
LEFT JOIN cited_work_members cm ON cm.full_mention_pk = m.full_mention_pk
LEFT JOIN cited_works w ON w.cited_work_pk = cm.cited_work_pk
WHERE v.stem = :stem AND m.kind IN ('ibid', 'op_cit', 'loc_cit', 'short') ORDER BY m.reading_ord

most_cited_works.title: Cited-reference index: most cited works, books included
most_cited_works.description: Times cited per cited work: citing articles (the Web-of-Science headline) and every mention, back references included; with the archive/catalogue record when one is linked.
most_cited_works.sql:
SELECT w.cited_work_id, w.pub_type, w.title, w.first_author_key, w.year_printed, w.year_calendar,
       t.n_citing_pubs, t.n_mentions, t.n_full, t.n_backrefs, l.target_pub_id AS in_mandumah,
       (SELECT group_concat(relation || ' ' || object_pub_id, '; ') FROM work_relations r
        WHERE r.subject_cited_work_pk = w.cited_work_pk) AS relations
FROM v_times_cited t JOIN cited_works w USING (cited_work_pk)
LEFT JOIN citation_links l ON l.cited_work_pk = w.cited_work_pk AND l.status = 'accepted' AND l.best = 1
ORDER BY t.n_citing_pubs DESC, t.n_mentions DESC LIMIT 200

corrections_ledger.title: The corrections ledger: what Azure read, what the page says, what is proposed
corrections_ledger.description: Azure misreadings fixed in the text (Azure's reading and confidence kept) and suspected misprints kept as printed with a proposed correction (D30), each on its ink.
corrections_ledger.sql:
SELECT v.stem, c.layer, c.xml_id, c.azure_reading, c.azure_wc, c.printed, c.proposed, c.why, c.block_id,
       c.anchor_method, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || c.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM text_corrections c JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = c.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
WHERE (:stem = '' OR v.stem = :stem) AND (:layer = '' OR c.layer = :layer)
ORDER BY v.stem, c.corr_pk LIMIT 1000

metadata_as_printed_and_corrected.title: Metadata as printed, as corrected (D33) and as catalogued
metadata_as_printed_and_corrected.description: Every reading of every field of one publication; the chosen one is marked with the rule that chose it.
metadata_as_printed_and_corrected.sql:
SELECT a.field, a.form, a.value, a.is_chosen, a.chosen_rule, a.reason, a.rule, v.run,
       'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || a.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM metadata_assertions a LEFT JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = a.version_id
WHERE a.pub_id = (SELECT pub_id FROM documents WHERE stem = :stem)
ORDER BY a.field, a.is_chosen DESC, a.form

catalogue_reports_for_mandumah.title: Catalogue reports for Mandumah (print vs catalogue, record problems)
catalogue_reports_for_mandumah.description: Who is right, the evidence on the page, and the status of each report.
catalogue_reports_for_mandumah.sql:
SELECT kind, field, stem, c999, catalogue_value, our_value, who_is_right, severity, evidence, note,
       status, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || anchor_pk AS ink
FROM catalogue_reports WHERE (:kind = '' OR kind = :kind) ORDER BY kind, stem LIMIT 1000

catalogue_reports_summary.title: Catalogue reports by kind and who is right
catalogue_reports_summary.sql: SELECT kind, who_is_right, count(*) AS n FROM catalogue_reports GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC

quran_index.title: Quran citation index: each aya, how often and by how many documents
quran_index.sql:
SELECT q.sura, a.sura_name_ar, q.aya_from, q.aya_to, q.n_places, q.n_documents
FROM v_quran_index q JOIN quran_ayat a ON a.sura = q.sura AND a.aya = q.aya_from
ORDER BY q.n_places DESC, q.sura, q.aya_from

quran_places.title: Every place the Quran is quoted or cited (with the ink)
quran_places.sql:
SELECT v.stem, q.source_kind, q.method, q.sura, a.sura_name_ar, q.aya_from, q.aya_to, q.printed_ref,
       q.quoted_text, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || q.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM quran_citations q JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = q.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
LEFT JOIN quran_ayat a ON a.sura = q.sura AND a.aya = q.aya_from
WHERE (:sura = '' OR q.sura = cast(:sura AS INTEGER)) ORDER BY q.sura, q.aya_from LIMIT 1000

search_arabic.title: Search (folded, clitics stripped): blocks, figure texts, equations, verses, citations
search_arabic.description: Type the words as printed (hamza, ta marbuta, vowels and و/ب/ال are handled); each hit opens its ink.
search_arabic.sql:
SELECT v.stem, u.unit_kind, u.unit_id, u.text, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || u.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM search_fts f JOIN search_units u ON u.uid = f.rowid JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = u.version_id
WHERE search_fts MATCH 'stemmed : ' || stem47(:q) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 200

verse_search.title: Verse index: vowelled verse lines, searched without vowels
verse_search.sql:
SELECT v.stem, l.verse_id, l.text, l.poet_hint, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || l.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM verse_lines l JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = l.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
WHERE l.text_bare LIKE '%' || fold(:q) || '%' LIMIT 300

least_trusted_blocks.title: Least trusted text (trust from Azure confidence, fixes, flags, retries)
least_trusted_blocks.sql:
SELECT v.stem, b.block_id, b.role, b.trust, b.wc_min, b.n_fixes, b.n_flags, b.text_source,
       substr(b.text, 1, 160) AS text, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || b.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM blocks b JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = b.version_id AND v.is_current = 1
WHERE b.trust IS NOT NULL ORDER BY b.trust, b.wc_min LIMIT 300

author_self_citations.title: True self-citation (the same person id cites their own work)
author_self_citations.sql:
SELECT s.citing_pub_id, p.title_shown, s.person_id, pe.preferred_name_ar, w.title AS cited_work
FROM v_author_self_citations s JOIN publications p ON p.pub_id = s.citing_pub_id
JOIN persons pe ON pe.person_id = s.person_id JOIN cited_works w USING (cited_work_pk)

person_by_name.title: A person by any form of the name (Arabic or Latin), with authorships
person_by_name.sql:
SELECT pe.person_id, pe.status, pe.preferred_name_ar, pe.preferred_name_lat,
       (SELECT group_concat(authority_id) FROM person_authorities pa WHERE pa.person_id = pe.person_id) AS authority,
       a.pub_id, p.title_shown, a.role_code, a.method, a.score
FROM persons pe JOIN authorships a USING (person_id) JOIN publications p ON p.pub_id = a.pub_id
WHERE pe.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM person_names WHERE name_key LIKE '%' || replace(fold(:name), ' ', '') || '%')
ORDER BY pe.person_id

versions_side_by_side.title: One document read by every run: versions, why one is shown, cost, flags
versions_side_by_side.sql:
SELECT v.version_id, v.run, r.kind, v.is_current, v.current_reason, v.complete, v.pages_covered, v.usd,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM blocks b WHERE b.version_id = v.version_id) AS blocks,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM text_corrections c WHERE c.version_id = v.version_id) AS corrections,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM flags f WHERE f.version_id = v.version_id) AS flags,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM citation_mentions m WHERE m.version_id = v.version_id) AS citation_mentions
FROM versions v JOIN runs r USING (run) WHERE v.stem = :stem ORDER BY v.version_id

flags_on_the_ink.title: Flags and judge findings of a document, each on its ink
flags_on_the_ink.sql:
SELECT 'flag' AS what, v.run, f.page, f.kind AS type, f.severity AS level, f.reason AS text, f.block_id,
       'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || f.anchor_pk AS ink
FROM flags f JOIN versions v USING (version_id) WHERE v.stem = :stem
UNION ALL
SELECT 'judge', c.run, c.page, j.type, j.route, j.evidence, NULL, 'http://127.0.0.1:8003/diagram/ink.html?a=' || j.anchor_pk
FROM judge_findings j JOIN judge_calls c USING (call_id) WHERE c.stem = :stem ORDER BY 3
